Why is it called ""One Source""?
All the wheat and water used to make Absolut comes from the Åhus area of southern Sweden, and every step from growing the grain to bottling happens in one place — the company's own term for this is ""One Source.""

What makes continuous distillation different?
Founder Lars Olsson Smith introduced it to Sweden in 1879, distilling the spirit far more times than the standard three or four pot-still passes used elsewhere at the time, for a purer, more consistent result.

Why is there a man's portrait on the bottle?
That's Lars Olsson Smith himself, nicknamed ""the Vodka King"" in Sweden — his medallion has appeared on every bottle since the brand's earliest days.

What makes Tennessee whiskey different from bourbon?
Both start from a similar corn-forward mash, but Tennessee whiskey is filtered through sugar maple charcoal before ageing — the Lincoln County Process. That step softens the spirit and gives Jack Daniel's its signature smooth character.

How should I store an opened bottle?
Keep it upright, out of direct sunlight, at room temperature. An opened bottle holds its character well for a year or more if the cap stays tight.

Is Jack Daniel's gluten-free?
Distillation removes gluten proteins, so the finished spirit contains none by the time it's bottled — though as a grain-derived product it isn't formally labelled gluten-free in every market.

Forty years before it had a name, it had a promise: consistency, whisky after whisky, blend after blend. Johnnie Walker Black Label is that promise, twelve years in the making.

John Walker began blending in a small grocer's shop in Kilmarnock, Ayrshire, in 1820. What started as a way to smooth out the inconsistency of single malt casks became the foundation of the world's most travelled Scotch. Black Label carries that founding idea forward — single malt and grain whiskies from across Scotland, each held back until it reaches at least twelve years old, before they're allowed anywhere near the blend.
🏆Gold — San Francisco World Spirits Competition
Rich and rounded — sweet vanilla up front, giving way to orange peel, dried raisin, and a background of gentle spice.
Full and smooth. The sweetness carries through, joined by baked fruit and a warming layer of smoke that never overpowers it.
Long, with lingering peat, malt, and a final wisp of smoke — the signature of the peated malts at its core.

Why is Black Label's age statement unusual?
Most blended whiskies state the age of only the youngest component. Black Label's 12-year statement applies to every single malt and grain whisky in the blend — a stricter standard than most competitors at this price point.

Is Black Label smoky?
Yes, moderately. Peated malts including Lagavulin and Talisker sit at its core, giving a background smokiness that builds through the palate into the finish, without dominating the sweeter, fruitier notes.

How should I serve it?
Neat or with a single large ice cube to open up the aromatics. It also holds its own in a classic Whisky Highball or Old Fashioned.

What is grappa made from?
Pomace — the skins, pulp and seeds left after grapes are pressed for wine. It is the ultimate use-everything spirit, and when the pomace is fresh and the distillation careful, it captures the grape more directly than wine itself can.

Isn't grappa supposed to be harsh?
Cheap grappa can be. That reputation comes from spoiled pomace and crude distillation. Poli take the skins within two days of pressing and distil them gently over a water bath — the result is aromatic, clean and genuinely elegant. It converts sceptics regularly.

Should I serve it ice cold?
No — that is a habit from hiding rough spirit. Around 12°C, in a tulip glass, is right. Cold enough to feel refreshing, warm enough that the blackberry and violet actually come through.

Who is this a good gift for?
Anyone who loves Italy, anyone who has enjoyed grappa in a restaurant and never bought a bottle, and any host who serves proper dinners. The distinctive squat Poli bottle also looks like exactly what it is — something chosen with care.

What does ""single pot still"" actually mean?
It is a uniquely Irish style: a mash of both malted and unmalted barley, distilled in copper pot stills at a single distillery. The raw barley is what gives it that thick, oily, slightly spicy texture you won't find in a single malt.

How is it different from ordinary Irish whiskey?
Most Irish whiskey on the shelf is a blend, softened with light grain spirit. This is the undiluted style — richer, weightier and far more characterful, matured for twelve years in sherry and bourbon wood.

Is it a good bottle for a Scotch drinker?
Very. Anyone who enjoys sherried Speyside whisky will recognise the dried fruit and spice immediately, then notice the extra oiliness that pot still brings. It converts sceptics faster than almost any other Irish bottle.

Who is this a good gift for?
The whiskey drinker who already owns the obvious bottles. It is widely regarded as the benchmark of its category, so it lands as a knowledgeable choice rather than a safe one — and it works equally well for a milestone birthday, a thank-you or a Christmas gift.

What is baijiu?
China's national spirit, distilled from grain — usually sorghum — using a solid-state fermentation process with a starter culture called qū. It is by volume the most consumed spirit category on earth, and almost unknown in most British homes.

Is this sweet?
No — the opposite. Seco means dry, and Alfonso is completely dry. The confusion is understandable: most sherry sold in Britain for decades was sweetened cream sherry, which is a different product entirely. A dry oloroso is closer in spirit to a serious white wine than to anything sugary.

What is the difference between fino and oloroso?
Flor. Fino is fortified lightly, so a living yeast cap survives on the surface and shields the wine from air — keeping it pale and delicate. Oloroso is fortified harder, the flor dies, and the wine ages in contact with oxygen instead. That is what makes it dark, nutty and full-bodied.

How long does it keep once opened?
Because it has already aged oxidatively, it is far more robust than a fino. Recorked and kept somewhere cool it will hold up well for a month or more — much longer than an ordinary white wine.

Anyone curious about the sherry revival, anyone who cooks Spanish food, and anyone who has run out of interesting things to drink before dinner. It also works well for someone who likes dry, savoury, nutty flavours — the sort of person who orders the olives first.
